title: Cross-border evaluation and fallback allocator for EU residency traffic
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Implement a routing subsystem that evaluates cross-border eligibility for each request and allocates fallback model variants when strict EU-only residency or tenant-level denylists prevent primary routing. This ticket covers the decision logic, tenant-scoped exemptions, audit hooks, and a lightweight allocator that selects the best permissible variant (region, tier, or quantized model) without violating residency constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Requests with EU-only residency flags must never egress to non-EU regions unless a documented emergency exemption exists
Tenant allowlist/denylist checks evaluate in O(1) for cached tenants and have documented cache invalidation semantics
Fallback allocator returns a compatible model variant that preserves API contract and indicates which constraint caused the fallback in response metadata
Audit log includes tenant id, routing decision, chosen region/tier/model, and policy version for every routed request
E2E tests cover at least three tenant profiles: EU-enforced, globally-allowed, and emergency-exempt
technical_design: Policy evaluation pipeline: request -> tenant policy fetch (cache) -> geography predicate -> tier eligibility -> fallback policy selector
Policy representation: normalized JSON pointers with precedence rules (tenant allowlist/denylist > account policy > global defaults)
Allocator strategy: weighted preference list (preferred-region, same-region-compatible-tier, quantized-local-variant, emergency-proxy) with fast short-circuiting
KV cache semantics: TTL 30s by default, invalidation on tenant policy update webhook from admin console
Audit hooks: synchronous shim that emits a compact routing event to Kafka with schema versioned per release
Compatibility mapping: model variants annotated with metadata (region affinity, tier, token-limit, quantization-compatibility) stored in model-catalog service
implementation_steps: 1) Add tenant policy cache interface and local in-memory LRU with metrics
2) Implement geography predicate and residency verifier as a reusable library
3) Build fallback allocator module with unit tests for policy precedence and tie-breaking
4) Wire audit event emission and add integration test to verify payload fields
5) Add admin console endpoints to mark emergency-exemptions and version policies
6) End-to-end smoke test using synthetic tenants and deploy to staging with canary rollout
progress_updates: 2025-02-13 — Kickoff: defined requirements with PM (Lena Ortiz) and Compliance (R. Novak). Agreed on audit fields and emergency exemption model.
2025-02-20 — Spike complete: prototype allocator passed latency budget in bench tests (median add < 0.6ms) — Carlos V. implemented cache interface.
2025-02-25 — Design sync: opted for short TTL + explicit invalidation rather than long TTL to reduce stale allowlist risk; Compliance requested additional audit fields.
2025-03-01 — PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4983 (fallback allocator + unit tests). Running CI; awaiting review from infra-team.
2025-03-03 — Manual integration: wired audit events into staging Kafka topic; observed events for synthetic EU tenant; minor schema tweak planned
review_feedback: Infra review: add circuit-breaker metric to avoid overload when model variants are exhausted
Compliance: require proof of no-ejection guarantee for EU-only tenants under normal operations; emergency exemption must be auditable and time-boxed
Design: prefer tenant-scoped override precedence over global defaults — already implemented in the prototype
risks_mitigation: Risk: cache staleness could allow incorrect routing — Mitigation: short TTL + policy change webhook + read-through validation for high-risk tenants
Risk: chosen fallback variant may degrade quality — Mitigation: tag fallbacks in response metadata and add monitoring/alerts for quality regressions
Risk: audit event loss could break compliance reporting — Mitigation: ensure at-least-once delivery to Kafka and durable storage of minimal routing trace
qa_plan: Unit tests for policy precedence and allocator tie-breakers
Integration tests that simulate policy changes and verify in-flight invalidation behavior
Staging end-to-end: route traffic for three synthetic tenant profiles and assert routing decisions and audit events
Chaos test: simulate model pool depletion to confirm graceful fallback and alerting
rollout_plan: Canary: 5% of routing traffic in staging -> validate audit logs and success metrics
Gradual: increase to 50% over 48 hours with automated rollback on error-rate > 0.5% or policy-violation detection
GA: 100% after 72 hours and postmortem review of canary metrics
Admin docs: update console runbook and provide a one-click revoke for emergency exemptions
notes: This ticket focuses on routing decision logic and allocator behavior only — infra autoscaling for Dedicated capacity will be a separate ticket
We intentionally avoid introducing new tenant storage shards; tenant policies are read from existing policy service to reduce scope
Coordinate with support on messaging when fallback occurs so customers understand potential quality tradeoffs
